title: The US Just Recorded Its First 2 Measles Deaths This Year
gist: Two unvaccinated Pennsylvanians died of measles amid a 35-year US case high (nearly 2,800 cases in 2026, up from 285 in 2023), with the outbreak concentrated in under-vaccinated communities as nonmedical exemption rates hit a record 4.2 percent and the Trump administration moves to split the MMR vaccine into separate doses over the objection of 210+ medical organizations.

themes.theme: Vaccination decline driving a measles resurgence

insights.claim: US measles cases have risen sharply year over year: 285 in 2023, 2,289 in 2025, and nearly 2,800 in 2026 so far, marking a 35-year high, per CDC data.
insights.speaker: Emily Mullin
entities: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
insights.so_what: A roughly 10x case increase in three years is a hard, trackable trendline for public-health forecasting and for any analysis of healthcare-system burden or vaccine-policy risk premiums.
insights.locator: Nationwide, there have been nearly 2,800 measles cases this year

insights.claim: Nonmedical vaccine exemptions among US kindergartners rose from 3.6 percent to a record 4.2 percent nationwide, while overall childhood vaccination coverage declined for all reported vaccines in the most recent school year, per new CDC data.
insights.speaker: Emily Mullin
entities: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
insights.so_what: Rising nonmedical exemption rates are the direct, quantified driver identified for the case surge — a leading indicator that outbreak risk (and associated public-health and healthcare-cost exposure) will likely keep climbing before it falls, since exemption trends move slowly.
insights.locator: Declining vaccination rates across the country are fueling

insights.claim: Measles requires roughly 95 percent community vaccination coverage to prevent outbreaks (herd immunity threshold), but Lancaster County, Pennsylvania has only 87 percent of incoming kindergartners fully vaccinated.
insights.speaker: Emily Mullin
insights.so_what: An 8-point gap below the herd-immunity threshold in a specific, named county gives a concrete, falsifiable local marker analysts can watch for recurrence, and quantifies how far coverage would need to rise to structurally end local outbreaks.
insights.locator: Measles is so contagious that 95 percent of a community needs to be vaccinated

insights.claim: President Trump signed an executive order to split the combined MMR vaccine into separate shots, which would require up to six doctor visits instead of two to complete the series; more than 210 medical organizations and patient groups issued a joint statement warning this would leave children less protected, and the article states there is no scientific basis for the split.
insights.speaker: Emily Mullin
insights.so_what: A federally mandated shift from 2 to up to 6 required visits is a direct friction increase on vaccination completion rates, which — combined with already-rising exemption rates — plausibly accelerates rather than reverses the current outbreak trend; a concrete near-term policy-to-outcome link to monitor.
insights.quote: The MMR vaccine has been licensed since 1971 as a single injection, and there is no scientific basis for separating it into separate vaccines.
insights.locator: Amid surging measles cases, President Donald Trump

insights.claim: Pennsylvania governor Josh Shapiro publicly rebuffed an outreach call from HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., telling him directly that Kennedy's rhetoric and actions are having a negative impact on communities, after Kennedy characterized outbreak areas as 'almost all religious communities that just don't vaccinate.'
insights.speaker: Emily Mullin
insights.so_what: An on-record state-versus-federal clash over vaccine messaging signals continuing political conflict between state health authorities and HHS leadership on immunization policy, a durable source of policy uncertainty for public-health and biotech/vaccine-adjacent stakeholders.
insights.quote: I made very clear that his actions and the rhetoric that's coming from this administration are having a negative impact on communities across America.
insights.locator: The governor said he was late to the press conference

insights.claim: Pennsylvania has logged 393 measles cases in 2026, roughly half in Lancaster County, with about 20 percent of infected individuals hospitalized statewide; only Utah and South Carolina have recorded more cases nationally this year.
insights.speaker: Emily Mullin
insights.so_what: A near-20% hospitalization rate quantifies the real clinical burden of this outbreak (versus a mild-illness assumption), relevant to hospital-capacity and healthcare-cost modeling in affected states.
insights.locator: Pennsylvania has recorded 393 measles cases in 2026

insights.claim: Pennsylvania's health department ran 91 pop-up vaccination clinics and administered over 4,100 vaccines statewide this year in response to the outbreak, with roughly a quarter of those doses given in Lancaster County alone.
insights.speaker: Emily Mullin
insights.so_what: This is a measurable state-level public-health response scale, useful as a benchmark for evaluating whether rapid-response vaccination campaigns are sufficient to reverse a specific county's coverage gap.
insights.locator: Shapiro said staff at the state health department have held 91 pop-up vaccination clinics
